head: c9840b2

smoke.cmd: npm test (= node --test test/organ.test.mjs); plus npm run demo and npm run demo:rewind
smoke.verdict: PASS 44/44 (145ms) + boot-demo PASS + rewind-demo 7/7 stages PASS (all offline)
smoke.notes: Suite = 34 v0/v1 tests untouched + 10 v2 (signed checkpoints, partial custody). Demos re-ran fresh this lane and wrote their receipts (examples/receipts/boot-demo-receipt.json, rewind-v1-demo-receipt.json); rewind demo stage 6 shows self-consistent padding caught as DOUBLE_ENTRY_REWIND_INVALID + DOUBLE_ENTRY_HASH_MISMATCH. No network, no API keys.

essence: Organ protocol v0→v2: verified custody bundles, rewind family, double-entry nesting, signed checkpoints.

ideas.name: custody bundle as content-addressed claim
ideas.statement: A bundle {manifest, state, receipts} is exactly the bytes needed to prove its own custody: snapshots are addressed by sha256 of canonicalized state plus the receipt-chain range; manifestHash self-covers the manifest minus itself; a snapshot that cannot recompute its own hashes is not a snapshot (spec §2 I1, §3).

ideas.name: the boot courtroom
ideas.statement: Boot is a courtroom where the custody claim is proven or thrown out: manifest law → carried state hashes → chain verify → custody anchor → replay == carried state, and boot never partially succeeds — the organ instance is constructed only after every check passes (spec §4). REPLAY_DIVERGENCE is the invariant that catches forgeries that re-hash themselves.

ideas.name: the rewind family + all-or-nothing transactions
ideas.statement: stateAt (pure time-travel with provenance), rewind (bundle = pure view; organ = custody-continuous truncation then continuation on the same hash chain), transact (PREPARE on detached copies against post-op state, COMMIT materializes once and self-verifies) — and a rewind does not erase: the host appends an evidence-carrying organ.rewind receipt that revokes credits, double-entry applied backwards (spec §7).

ideas.name: nesting envelope + double-entry law
ideas.statement: A nested organ keeps its own unbroken hash chain while the host ledger receives credit receipts pointing at organ debits; every post-nest debit has exactly one live host credit and every credit resolves to a real debit whose replayed hash matches — verifyDoubleEntry reports fail-closed, never auto-repairs (spec §5).

ideas.name: signed checkpoints make the custody gap conditional
ideas.statement: signCheckpoint replays the prefix once and HMACs the canonical triple {hash, manifestHash, seq}; the signature anchors the replay seed through two content-address hops (sig → manifestHash → prefix manifest → seed); boot from partial custody is legal iff a valid signature covers the boundary — unsigned gaps still fail closed, and below the floor even stateAt/rewind refuse REWIND_PAST_CUSTODY (spec §8).

parts.name: canonicalJson (fail-closed)
parts.essence: Recursive key-sorted UTF-8 no-whitespace serialization that throws on values with no stable JSON meaning (undefined, functions, NaN) at the exact path — the form every hash is taken over.
parts.gate: undefined / functions / NaN refuse to serialize (throw)
parts.failure_mode: STATE_UNSERIALIZABLE downstream when staged state has no canonical form

parts.name: receipt hash formula
parts.essence: receiptHash = sha256(canonical({seq, op, prev})) with op an OBJECT carrying all effect content; receipts carry no wall-clock time — seq is time.
parts.gate: recomputed hash must equal carried hash

parts.name: per-cell + cells-map state hashes
parts.essence: cellStateHash = sha256Json({kind, value}); cellsStateHash = sha256 over canonical cells map — the manifest carries both, so state tampering is loud at cell granularity and whole-state granularity.
parts.gate: recomputed hashes must equal manifest claims

parts.name: manifestHash self-cover
parts.essence: manifestHash = sha256(canonical(manifest minus manifestHash)); organId = name@16-hex minted once and carried forward; supersedes pins the prior manifest for re-snapshots.
parts.gate: recomputed self-cover must equal carried manifestHash

parts.name: deterministic op evaluator (toyQuilt)
parts.essence: applyOp cells→cells for the op set; deterministic, no clock, no randomness — the engine that makes replay == carried state a meaningful assertion at all.
parts.gate: an op must be determinable and reference known cells

parts.name: verifyChain (contiguity + linkage)
parts.essence: Walks the carried receipts: seq continuity from expectedStart, prev == previous hash, recomputed hash == carried hash, count == receiptRange; a gap is a missing page of custody.
parts.gate: chain is contiguous and parent-bound across the full window

parts.name: snapshot() freezing
parts.essence: Freezes {manifest, state, receipts} into the portable bundle — content-addressed, supersedes-linked, count-consistent; snapshotOrgan re-snapshots a booted organ carrying its ledger.
parts.gate: frozen bundle must pass its own validation

parts.name: pre-verb courtroom
parts.essence: Every rewind-family verb (stateAt/rewind/transact) re-runs the full courtroom on the subject BEFORE acting: chain verify + replay == carried state, bundle or booted organ alike — a rewind cannot become a forgery laundromat for the tail it ignores.
parts.gate: no verb acts on an unproven subject

parts.name: replay == carried assertion
parts.essence: The courtroom's final invariant: replaying the receipt range over the replay base (empty cells, or the anchored seed) must hash-equal manifest.state.cellsSha256 — replay divergence is a hard stop, not a warning.
parts.gate: replayed state hash == carried state hash

parts.name: manifest schema law
parts.essence: validateManifest refuses unknown schema/schemaVersion (never best-effort parse), malformed fields, bad hex, edges to unknown cells — future formats extend via schemaVersion with fail-closed drift.
parts.gate: schema + schemaVersion are exactly the implemented ones

parts.name: custody anchor policy
parts.essence: v0 trusts exactly two anchors: GENESIS and an explicit checkpoint {seq,hash}; an unanchored prefix (range starts at seq>0, no checkpoint) is unowned history; v2 narrows this: a seed-bearing gap is legal only under a verified signature — contradictory custody claims (seed + genesis.seq 0) refuse.
parts.gate: every carried range must be anchored; every gap must be signature-covered

parts.name: rewind bounds policy
parts.essence: toSeq must be an integer within [carried range start, tip]: below the carried start is unowned history (naming the checkpoint boundary under partial custody), beyond the tip is not a rewind — advance by boot+append instead.
parts.gate: toSeq within the subject's carried custody

parts.name: transact atomicity
parts.essence: PREPARE stages every op on detached copies, each validated against the post-op state of the ops before it; first failure returns {ok:false, phase:prepare, failedOp, code} with the input byte-untouched; COMMIT materializes the successor exactly once via snapshot() and self-verifies it through verifyBundle — no partially-extended bundle ever exists.
parts.gate: all ops or nothing; successor passes its own boot courtroom

parts.name: double-entry balance law
parts.essence: Every LIVE host credit must resolve to a debit the organ's carried ledger holds (same seq, same debitHash) and every carried post-nest debit must be covered by a live credit; verify-only, never auto-repair; returns creditsChecked/creditsRevoked/rewinds.
parts.gate: debits and credits net to zero across the nest boundary

parts.name: compensating rewind receipt (revocation law)
parts.essence: Rewinding past a nest boundary appends ONE host receipt organ.rewind carrying rewound[] evidence; append-only evidence-based revocation (nothing erased), self-audit (every entry must match a real credit), temporal form (listed creditSeq must precede the rewind receipt's own seq — making self-consistent padding structurally impossible since the evidence hash depends on the receipt hash that depends on the evidence).
parts.gate: evidence must be real, unique, and temporally precede the receipt

parts.name: checkpoint signature policy
parts.essence: verifySignedCheckpoint checks structure (schema/version/alg/seq/hash/manifestHash/sig), refuses unknown algorithms (Ed25519 is v3, not a fallback), and HMACs canonical({hash, manifestHash, seq}) under the verifier's key — the only trust input is the key.
parts.gate: unknown alg refuses; HMAC must verify under the provided key

parts.name: carve policy
parts.essence: carvePartialCustody is keyless and mechanical: it re-derives the prefix manifest from the verified full bundle, refuses a checkpoint that does not describe this bundle's prefix exactly, refuses carving at the tip (no tail would remain), and emits the partial bundle [seq+1..tip] + seed + signed checkpoint.
parts.gate: checkpoint prefix must re-hash to the signed manifestHash; boundary must leave a tail

parts.name: signCheckpoint mint
parts.essence: Minting verifies the bundle through the full boot courtroom first (never sign an unproven snapshot), replays the prefix ONCE, snapshots it, and signs the triple — refusing partial-custody sources and out-of-range boundaries.
outputs: signed checkpoint {schema, alg, seq, hash, manifestHash, sig, manifest}
parts.gate: never sign an unproven snapshot; boundary within carried range; full custody source

parts.name: seed-aware replay base
parts.essence: stateAt/rewind/transact and verifyDoubleEntry all accept the partial-custody seed as the replay floor: prefix queries answer hash-equal to the full bundle's answers above the floor; the seed is re-verified against the boot-time custody hash on every use.
parts.gate: seed hash must equal the boot-verified custody seed hash

parts.name: boot()
parts.essence: The courtroom's only constructive exit: after every check passes, the organ wakes with state, organId, ledger append rights, and custody provenance — boot never partially succeeds.
parts.gate: constructed only after every check passes
parts.failure_mode: OrganBootError with the first failing code

parts.name: stateAt / rewind verbs
parts.essence: stateAt = pure time-travel query with provenance {start, end, count, tipHash}, never mutates, works on bundles and organs; rewind = pure view on bundles, destructive truncate+pure-replay-rebuild on organs, then continuation appends from the rewound tip on the SAME hash chain (custody unbroken).
parts.gate: same-chain continuation after organ rewind; purity on bundle subjects

parts.name: nestInto + credit append
parts.essence: nestInto boots the organ into the host: organ keeps its own chain, host receives organ.nest custody marker + organ.credit pointer receipts {organId, organSeq, debitHash, stateHashAfter} that add no organ state to the host; same manifestHash cannot nest twice.
parts.gate: host chain stays contiguous; one nest receipt per manifestHash

parts.name: custody provenance on the booted organ
parts.essence: A partial-custody organ wakes carrying organ.custody {kind: signed-checkpoint, signedAt {seq,hash,manifestHash,alg}, verifiedRange, seed {seq,cells,stateHash}} — what was signature-anchored and what replay actually verified travels with the organ.
parts.gate: provenance names the anchor the custody rests on

parts.name: fail-closed error table as law
parts.essence: §4 (v0, 11 rows) + §7.3 (v1, 7 rows) + §8.3 (v2, 8 rows) name every refusal; codes are stable and grep-able; the test suite proves each code fires (tamper trio, chain gap, replay divergence, rewind past custody, checkpoint forgery quartet).
parts.gate: every named code has a test or a refusal behind it
parts.failure_mode: SCHEMA_DRIFT | MANIFEST_INVALID | STATE_HASH_MISMATCH | RECEIPT_HASH_MISMATCH | CHAIN_GAP | CUSTODY_GAP | CUSTODY_CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH | REPLAY_DIVERGENCE | REPLAY_INVALID_OP | DUPLICATE_NEST | DOUBLE_ENTRY_* | REWIND_TARGET_INVALID | REWIND_PAST_CUSTODY | TRANSACTION_INVALID | OP_MALFORMED | OP_APPLY_FAILED | STATE_UNSERIALIZABLE | CHECKPOINT_* (26 distinct codes observed in src)

parts.name: demo receipts as sealed evidence
parts.essence: Both demos write receipt JSON files (boot-demo-receipt.json, rewind-v1-demo-receipt.json, rewind-v1-upload-receipt.json) so a run's claims are sealed artifacts, not console folklore — the L16 receipt-of-record discipline at example scale.
parts.gate: receipts are regenerated truthfully by the runs themselves
parts.evidence: examples/receipts/ (3 files); examples/rewind-demo.mjs; README.md ORGAN BOOT sections

cells.expr: sorted-keys UTF-8 serialization; throws on undefined/NaN/function at path
contiguity + prev linkage + hash recompute over the window
freeze {manifest, state, receipts} into a self-proving bundle
chain verify + replay==carried, re-run before ANY verb
manifest law → hashes → chain → anchor → replay; construct organ only if all pass
stateAt: pure prefix replay + provenance; rewind: pure view on bundles, truncate+rebuild+continue-same-chain on organs
PREPARE detached / COMMIT once via snapshot + self-verify
debits ↔ live credits balance; rewind evidence revocation; seed-aware
courtroom first, replay prefix once, HMAC canonical({hash,manifestHash,seq})
structure + alg allow-list + HMAC under key
re-derive prefix manifest, cut [seq+1..tip] + seed + signed checkpoint

layer_logic.0: Canonical JSON + sha256 content addressing over {seq, op, prev}, {kind, value}, and the manifest minus its self-hash — a custody claim is bytes that must re-derive themselves.
layer_logic.1: The deterministic evaluator + hash chains turn receipts into state: snapshot freezes, replay rebuilds, and the seed (under signature) replaces genesis as the replay floor for scale.
layer_logic.2: Policy is the courtroom docket: schema admission, custody anchors, rewind bounds, transaction atomicity, double-entry balance with evidence-based revocation, and signature coverage — every check fail-closed, verify-only, never auto-repair.
layer_logic.3: Interface = the verbs: boot (constructive exit), stateAt (pure query), rewind (pure view on bundles / custody-continuous truncation on organs), transact (all-or-nothing), nest (host credits), sign/carve (checkpoint custody).
layer_logic.4: Evidence = 26 distinct named error codes across three spec tables, custody provenance carried on the organ, demo receipts written by the runs, and a 44-test suite where every named code has a refusal or a passing proof behind it.
